butter.etymology_derivation: Borrowed together into West Germanic from Latin butyrum / Greek boutyron.

gold.context_phrase: Nicht alles, was glänzt, ist Gold.
gold.context_translation: Not all that glitters is gold.

sand.context_translation: The children play in the sand.

hunger.context_translation: I have great hunger / I am very hungry.

bier.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *beuzą. Medial ie produces pure tense monophthong [iː].

wein.etymology_derivation: Early Latin loanword vinum entered into both Old English and Old High German.

lernen.context_translation: I am learning German with Brücke.
lernen.etymology_derivation: Shared root *liznōną (to follow a track/learn) + infinitive -en.

finden.context_translation: I cannot find it / I find it not.
finden.etymology_derivation: Stem find + infinitive -en (German keeps pure short [ɪ] vowel).

singen.etymology_derivation: Initial S voiced to [z] before vowels.

bringen.etymology_derivation: Shared ancient Germanic mixed verb (bring/brought ↔ bringen/gebracht).

fisch.context_translation: The fish swims in the water.

wolf.context_translation: The wolf lives in the forest.

eis.context_translation: I would like to eat an ice cream / ice.

stein.context_phrase: Ein Stein liegt auf dem Weg.
stein.context_translation: A stone lies on the path.

denken.etymology_derivation: TH → D hardening. Shares the exact vowel-shift relationship with "danken" that English has in "think" and "thank" (a thank is a good thought).

danken.etymology_derivation: Danke is an ellipsis of "[Ich] danke [dir/Ihnen]".

bruder.etymology_derivation: Medial th shifted to d; unstressed -er vocalizes to [ɐ].

bad.etymology_derivation: Final th shifted to d (devoiced in pronunciation to [t]). Verb: baden (to bathe).

donner.etymology_derivation: TH → D hardening. Living in English "Thursday" (Thor's/Thunder's day = Donnerstag) and Santa's reindeer "Donner and Blitzen" (Thunder and Lightning).

du.etymology_derivation: Direct cognate of archaic English "thou". Conjugates with -st (thou goest ↔ du gehst).

das.shift_rule: TH → D + T → S / SS / Z
das.etymology_derivation: Double shift: th → d and final t → s.

die.etymology_derivation: th → d. Sounds identical to emphatic English "thee".

durst.context_translation: I have great thirst / I am very thirsty.

daumen.context_translation: I press my thumbs (I cross my fingers for you).

dieb.context_translation: The police are looking for the thief.
dieb.etymology_derivation: Double shift: th → d and f/v → b.

denn.context_phrase: Ich gehe, denn ich bin müde.
denn.context_translation: I am going, for / because I am tired.

durch.etymology_derivation: Double shift: th → d and gh → ch.

darm.context_phrase: Der Magen und der Darm verdauen das Essen.
darm.context_translation: The stomach and the intestine digest the food.

dach.context_phrase: Auf dem Dach sitzt ein Vogel.
dach.context_translation: A bird sits on the roof.
dach.etymology_derivation: Double shift: th → d and k/t → ch (thatch ↔ Dach).

tag.etymology_derivation: Double shift: d → t and y → g.

tür.etymology_derivation: d → t with vowel mutation to ü.

tief.etymology_derivation: Double shift: d → t and p → f.

trinken.context_translation: I drink a glass of water.

garten.context_translation: The children play in the garden.

tochter.context_phrase: Meine Tochter lernt in der Schule.
tochter.etymology_derivation: Double shift: d → t and gh → ch.

wort.etymology_derivation: Final d → t. Plural: Wörter / Worte.

tun.context_translation: I am sorry (literally: it does sorrow to me).

tisch.context_phrase: Der Teller steht auf dem Tisch.
tisch.context_translation: The plate stands on the table.
tisch.etymology_derivation: Latin discus → Old English disc (dish/desk) → Old High German tisc (tisch, with d → t).

tropfen.context_translation: A drop of water fell down.
tropfen.etymology_derivation: Double shift: d → t and p → pf.

treiben.shift_rule: D → T + V / F → B + Ablaut Vowels
treiben.context_translation: What are you up to / driving at today?
treiben.etymology_derivation: Double shift: d → t and v → b.

treu.context_phrase: Ein treuer Freund ist viel wert.
treu.context_translation: A faithful friend is worth a lot.

tot.etymology_derivation: Double shift: initial d → t and final d → t (dead → tot).

tod.etymology_derivation: d → t and th → d (death ↔ Tod).

taube.etymology_derivation: Double shift: d → t and v → b.

taub.context_phrase: Er ist auf einem Ohr taub.
taub.context_translation: He is deaf in one ear.
taub.etymology_derivation: Double shift: d → t and f/v → b.

tal.context_phrase: Der Fluss fließt durch das Tal.
tal.context_translation: The river flows through the valley / dale.

tau.context_phrase: Morgens liegt Tau auf dem Gras.
tau.context_translation: In the morning dew lies on the grass.

teil.etymology_derivation: d → t (cognate with English "deal" as in a great deal / dole).

tausend.context_translation: The book has a thousand pages.
tausend.etymology_derivation: Initial th → t and final d → t [t].

teufel.context_translation: The devil is in the details.

helfen.etymology_derivation: p → f. Governs the dative case (mir).

schlafen.etymology_derivation: p → f with sl- → schl- cluster.

pfeffer.context_phrase: Gib mir bitte Salz und Pfeffer.
pfeffer.context_translation: Please give me salt and pepper.
pfeffer.etymology_derivation: Double shift: initial p → pf and medial pp → ff.

pflanze.shift_rule: P → PF / F + T → S / SS / Z
pflanze.etymology_derivation: Double shift: initial p → pf and t → z [ts].

schiff.etymology_derivation: P → FF shift. Cognate with English "ship" and living nautical twin "skipper" (literally Schiff-er, ship-master).

pfeife.etymology_derivation: Double shift: initial p → pf and medial p → f.

pfad.etymology_derivation: Double shift: initial p → pf and th → d.

pfanne.context_phrase: Das Essen brät in der Pfanne.
pfanne.context_translation: The food is frying in the pan.

pfund.etymology_derivation: Double shift: p → pf and final d → t [t].

pforte.context_translation: We stand before the gate / portal.

greifen.context_translation: He grasps / grips for my hand.

dampf.context_phrase: Aus dem Topf steigt Dampf auf.
dampf.context_translation: Steam rises out of the pot.

treffen.etymology_derivation: Double shift: d → t and p → ff (cognate with English "drap" / strike).

essen.shift_rule: T → S / SS / Z + Ablaut Vowels
essen.context_translation: What do we want to eat?
essen.etymology_derivation: Medial t → ss. Noun: das Essen (food).

aus.context_translation: I come from / out of Berlin.

zu.etymology_derivation: Initial t → z [ts]. Functions as both intensifier (too) and infinitive particle (in order to).

groß.etymology_derivation: T → S/ß shift from Germanic "great". Preserved in English "gross income", "gross national product", and "a gross error" (large, not disgusting).

straße.etymology_derivation: Roman paved road (via strata) gave English "street" (kept Latin "t") and German "Straße" (shifted "t" to sharp "ß").

weiß.etymology_derivation: t → ß. Also first-person of wissen (ich weiß = I know/am wise).

sitzen.shift_rule: T → S / SS / Z + Ablaut Vowels
sitzen.context_translation: We are sitting in the café.

katze.context_phrase: Die Katze schläft auf dem Sofa.
katze.context_translation: The cat sleeps on the sofa.

zeit.etymology_derivation: t → z [ts] (cognate with English "tide", as in Yuletide or time and tide).

zehe.context_phrase: Ich habe mir die Zehe gestoßen.

zinn.context_translation: The goblet is made of tin.

ziehen.shift_rule: T → S / SS / Z + Ablaut Vowels
ziehen.etymology_derivation: t → z [ts] (Proto-Germanic *teuhaną, cognate with English tow / tug).

brechen.context_phrase: Ich will das Glas nicht brechen.
brechen.context_translation: I do not want to break the glass.
brechen.etymology_derivation: k → ch (Ich-Laut [ç] after front vowel e).

suchen.context_translation: I am looking for my glasses.
suchen.etymology_derivation: k → ch. Direct transitive object without prepositions.

buch.context_translation: I am reading a good book.

woche.context_phrase: Nächste Woche fahre ich nach Berlin.
woche.context_translation: Next week I travel to Berlin.

kirche.etymology_derivation: Greek kyriakon → Scottish kirk / German Kirche.

rauch.context_phrase: Wo Rauch ist, ist auch Feuer.
rauch.context_translation: Where there is smoke, there is also fire.

welch.etymology_derivation: k → ch (Old English hwelc ↔ German welch).

solch.etymology_derivation: k → ch (Old English swylc ↔ German solch).

bleich.context_phrase: Er wurde vor Schreck ganz bleich.
bleich.context_translation: He turned completely pale with fright.

küche.context_translation: We are cooking in the kitchen.

zeichen.shift_rule: T → S / SS / Z + K → CH
zeichen.context_translation: That is a good sign / token.
zeichen.etymology_derivation: Double shift: t → z and k → ch (token ↔ Zeichen).

sache.context_translation: That is my affair / thing (for my sake).

geben.context_translation: There is a problem (literally: it gives a problem).
geben.etymology_derivation: v → b. In impersonal form "es gibt", expresses existence.

glauben.etymology_derivation: be- ↔ ge- & lieve ↔ lauben (v → b). Governs dative case.

silber.context_translation: The ring is made of silver.

über.context_translation: We are speaking about / over the book.

halb.context_translation: It is half past seven (halfway to eight).

gelb.etymology_derivation: Double shift: y → g and w/v → b (yellow → gelb).

kalb.context_phrase: Die Kuh hat ein kleines Kalb.
kalb.context_translation: The cow has a small calf.

laub.context_phrase: Das bunte Laub fällt von den Bäumen.
laub.context_translation: The colorful foliage falls from the trees.

legen.context_phrase: Ich lege das Buch auf den Tisch.
legen.context_translation: I lay the book on the table.

liegen.context_phrase: Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch.
liegen.context_translation: The book lies on the table.

segel.context_phrase: Das weiße Segel weht im Wind.
segel.context_translation: The white sail blows in the wind.

nagel.context_phrase: Er schlägt den Nagel in die Wand.
nagel.context_translation: He hammers the nail into the wall.

fliege.context_translation: A fly buzzes in the room.

nacht.context_phrase: In der Nacht ist es hier sehr ruhig.
nacht.context_translation: At night it is very quiet here.

nachbar.etymology_derivation: nach (near) + bauer (dweller). Silent gh in neighbor preserves German ch.

knecht.context_phrase: Der Knecht arbeitet auf dem Hof.
knecht.context_translation: The farmhand works on the estate.
knecht.etymology_derivation: gh → ch (knight ↔ Knecht). In English it elevated to noble warrior; in German it remained farm servant.

reparieren.context_translation: I have to repair the television.

funktionieren.etymology_derivation: Used specifically for machines and mechanisms functioning properly.

kapieren.context_translation: Did you get it / grasp it?
kapieren.etymology_derivation: From Latin capere (to seize/capture). Mental grasp.

akzeptieren.etymology_derivation: Latin acceptare (hard c → k, soft c → z [ts]).

reduzieren.context_translation: We have to reduce the costs.
reduzieren.etymology_derivation: Soft Latin c shifted to German z [ts].

existieren.context_translation: The problem does not exist anymore.

argumentieren.etymology_derivation: Directly derived from the Latin noun base argumentum + -ieren.

reservieren.context_translation: I would like to reserve a table.

wollen.etymology_derivation: Retains original Germanic sense of desire/intent: "free will", "will to live", "against my will", and "willingly" (cf. Latin voluntary).

können.context_translation: I can come / I am able to come.
können.etymology_derivation: Originally meant "to know/understand". Preserved in English "can", "cunning" (knowing how), "uncanny", and "beyond my ken" (beyond my knowledge).

müssen.context_translation: I must / have to go now.
müssen.etymology_derivation: Cognate with English "must" (root shifted to sibilant -ss-).

dürfen.etymology_derivation: Double shift: th → d and p → f.

sollen.etymology_derivation: Direct twin of English "shall" and "should" (Shakespeare: "thou shalt" ↔ German "du sollst").

mögen.etymology_derivation: Cognate with English "may" and "might" (Proto-Germanic *maganą). Subjunctive: möchte (would like).

werden.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *werþaną (cognate with archaic English "worth" as in "woe worth the day").

zumachen.shift_rule: K → CH + T → S / SS / Z

mitnehmen.context_translation: I want to take the food away / to go.

aussuchen.shift_rule: T → S / SS / Z + K → CH
aussuchen.context_phrase: Du kannst dir ein Buch aussuchen.
aussuchen.context_translation: You can choose / seek out a book for yourself.

verstehen.etymology_derivation: Inseparable: ver- (for-) + stehen (stand). Past participle: verstanden (no ge-).

versuchen.context_translation: I am trying to find it.

begriff.etymology_derivation: Calque of Latin conceptus (con- + capere → be- + greifen/Griff = grasp together).

gegenstand.context_phrase: Ein kleiner Gegenstand liegt auf dem Tisch.
gegenstand.context_translation: A small object lies on the table.
gegenstand.etymology_derivation: Calque of Latin objectum (ob- + jacere → gegen- + Stand = standing against).

wahrnehmung.etymology_derivation: Calque of Latin perceptio (wahr = true + nehmen = take → taking as true).

rolle.etymology_derivation: Direct cognate from Latin rotula (little wheel / scroll of parchment for actors).

haus.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hūsą — an exact twin of English house, down to the diphthong. [wiktionary]

brot.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *braudą — originally "the fermented/risen thing", kin to the verb brew (German brauen). Bread is "the brewed thing". [wiktionary]

folgen.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *fulgāną — English softened the ancient g into w (follow), German kept it spelled out. Takes the dative. [wiktionary]

wandern.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *wandarōn — German kept the full -ern ending that English wore down to -er. [wiktionary]

warnen.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *warnōn — a parallel formation to English warn (Old English wearnian). [wiktionary]

hungern.etymology_derivation: Denominal verb from Hunger; English kept "to hunger" in older texts ("they hungered"). [wiktionary]

morgen.etymology_derivation: Cognate with English morrow (hence to-morrow) and morn — both descend from the Germanic root for "morning". [wiktionary]

pferd.etymology_derivation: Late Latin paraverēdus (a post-road saddle horse) — the same medieval loan that became English palfrey via French; German affricated p → pf, English kept p. [wiktionary]

zwilling.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *twinaz (two, twinned) + the Germanic suffix -ling (as in duckling); English twin is the same root without the suffix. [wiktionary]

zwerg.shift_rule: T → S / SS / Z + K → CH
zwerg.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *dwergaz — German hardened the ancient cluster dw- into zw- and final g into ch; English dwarf kept both. Double-shift word. [wiktionary]

zweimal.etymology_derivation: zwei (two) + Mal (time, cognate with English meal — the same word as in piecemeal, "one piece at a time"). [wiktionary]

zwanzig.etymology_derivation: zwei + -zig (German's ancient -ty, as in six-ty); the whole word is a double t → z shift of twenty. [wiktionary]

dieser.etymology_derivation: North Sea Germanic demonstrative: Old English þis and German dieser are one system — dies- ↔ this. [wiktionary]

mein.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *mīnaz — identical to English mine; the KJV's 'mine eyes' preserves the older use. [wiktionary]

kein.etymology_derivation: Back-formation of nekein 'not any' (ni + ein, 'not one') — built right on ein, exactly like English none ← 'not one'. [wiktionary]

nicht.etymology_derivation: OHG niowiht: 'never a creature/thing' — the same no-thing story as English not ← nāwiht, kin to archaic wight 'being'. The gh of naught survives as German ch. [wiktionary]

wo.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hwēr/*hwar — the exact twin of English where; English kept the h (wh-), German dropped it. [wiktionary]

wer.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hwaz — the exact twin of English who. The famous trap: wer asks WHO, wo asks WHERE. [wiktionary]

wann.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hwan — the exact twin of English when. [wiktionary]

wie.context_translation: How are you? (How goes it to you?)
wie.etymology_derivation: From Proto-Germanic *hwē, a fossilized instrumental of who/what — the same variant that gave English why. [wiktionary]

warum.etymology_derivation: wo + um — 'around-what / for-what', the structural twin of English wherefore ('for what'). [wiktionary]

wohin.context_translation: Where are you going (whither goest thou)?
wohin.etymology_derivation: wo + hin; hin is the twin of the h- in English hence/hither — 'to where' in one word. [wiktionary]

weil.context_translation: I learn because I want to.
weil.etymology_derivation: Not a Latin loan: a plain descendant of Proto-Germanic *hwīlō — the same word as English while. [wiktionary]

dass.context_translation: I know that you are coming.
dass.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *þat — the exact twin of English that, and a doublet of German das. [wiktionary]

aufwachen.etymology_derivation: Separable: auf (up) + wachen (to be awake/watch); wachen and wake are one verb — a shepherd 'wacht' the flock. [wiktionary]

zurückkommen.shift_rule: T → S / SS / Z + K → CH
zurückkommen.context_translation: We are coming back at eight.
zurückkommen.etymology_derivation: Separable: zu + Rücken (the back, cognate with ridge) + kommen — 'come to-the-back', the exact mirror of come back. [wiktionary]

verlieren.etymology_derivation: ver- (for-) + lieren from Proto-Germanic *leusaną — the same root as English lose; forlorn is 'utterly lost' (forleosan), the exact ver- construction. [wiktionary]

bekommen.etymology_derivation: be- (by/around) + kommen (come) — literally 'come by (something)'; English become is the same be + come with a different job. [wiktionary]

erinnern.etymology_derivation: er- (out/thorough) + innern (inner) — to 'internal-ize' a thing; built on inn(inner), the twin of English inner. [wiktionary]

erklären.etymology_derivation: er- (out) + klar (clear) — 'to make clear'; klar and clear are both medieval loans of Latin clarus. [wiktionary]

jener.context_translation: That man over there (yon man) is tall.
jener.etymology_derivation: The far demonstrative — the twin of archaic English yon/yonder (Proto-Germanic *jēnaz). [wiktionary]

elf.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *ainalif — 'one left over' after counting ten, the exact twin of eleven. [wiktionary]

zwölf.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *twalif — 'two left over', the exact tw → zw twin of twelve. [wiktionary]

dreißig.shift_rule: TH → D + T → S / SS / Z
dreißig.etymology_derivation: drei + the old -zig ending (English's -ty): thirty with th → d and t → ß — a double-shift number. [wiktionary]

heute.etymology_derivation: Literally 'on this day': heu- is the he- of here/him, and the old ending hid Tag (day). English's own twin hēodæġ died out — today won. [wiktionary]

genug.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *ganōgaz with the ancient ge- prefix — the same prefix English wore down to y- (yclept, ywis) and buried inside 'enough'. [wiktionary]

fahren.context_translation: I am going / driving to Berlin.
fahren.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *faraną — the twin of English fare (farewell, bus fare, 'how did you fare?'). [wiktionary]

nehmen.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *nemaną — the twin of archaic English nim 'to take', surviving in nimble ('quick to grasp'); English take is a Norse import. [wiktionary]

mir.context_translation: Can you please help me? (literally: help to me)
mir.etymology_derivation: Dative of ich — the same ancient pronoun as English me, keeping the 'to me' meaning (mir ist kalt = it is cold to me). [wiktionary]

mit.etymology_derivation: The exact twin of archaic English mid 'with' — fossilized in midwife, 'with-woman'. Governs the dative. [wiktionary]

bei.etymology_derivation: The exact twin of English by — both from Proto-Germanic *bi. Governs the dative. [wiktionary]

gefallen.context_translation: I like it (it falls well to me).
gefallen.etymology_derivation: ge- + fallen — 'to fall to someone' (by lot or liking), like English 'as it falls out'. Strong verb: gefiel, gefallen. [wiktionary]

ihm.etymology_derivation: Dative of er — the exact twin of English him; the h dropped from speech and stayed in spelling. [wiktionary]

uhr.etymology_derivation: Loan-cognate of hour (Latin hōra via French), and a distant doublet of Jahr and year (PIE *yóh₁r̥). German alone turned it into the word for the clock itself. [wiktionary]

schreiben.etymology_derivation: A Latin loan (scribere) that both languages Germanicized — English kept it in scribe, script, describe. Strong verb: schrieb, geschrieben. [wiktionary]

dir.etymology_derivation: Dative of du — the exact twin of archaic English 'I give it thee'; the dative is the giving case. [wiktionary]

montag.etymology_derivation: Moon-day: both name the day after the moon — English kept the moon's name, German kept the compound with Tag. [wiktionary]

dienstag.context_phrase: Der Dienstag kommt nach dem Montag.
dienstag.etymology_derivation: Day of the same god: Tuesday is Tiw's day (Tīwaz), Dienstag is the thing-god's day (Thingsus) — two names for one sky-god, th → d included. [wiktionary]

freitag.etymology_derivation: Frigg's/Freia's day — both languages named the day for the Germanic love goddess, spelled two ways. [wiktionary]

sonntag.etymology_derivation: Sun-day — the identical calque in both languages: the sun's day, t → z in the sun. [wiktionary]

mann.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *mann- — the identical twin of man; German keeps the short a English lengthened. [wiktionary]

frau.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *frawjǭ 'lady, mistress' — kin to archaic English frow 'lady'; Fräulein andMs.-style Frauennamen carry the same root. [wiktionary]

kind.context_translation: The child plays in the garden.
kind.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *kindą, related to the root of English kin — 'of the family'. The t → z shift never fired here; the d hardened to t instead. [wiktionary]

alt.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *aldaz — the twin of old; the l stayed, the vowel and final d/t report the shift. [wiktionary]

hoch.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hauhaz — the twin of high, with high's gh still sounding as the Ach-Laut ch. Comparative: höher (high→higher). [wiktionary]

mehr.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *maizô — the twin of more (and its cousin most/meist); the r survived, the vowel lengthened. [wiktionary]

unter.context_phrase: Die Katze ist unter dem Tisch.
unter.context_translation: The cat is under the table.
unter.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *undar — the exact twin of under; governs dative (location) and accusative (motion). [wiktionary]

vor.context_phrase: Das Auto steht vor dem Haus.
vor.context_translation: The car stands in front of the house.
vor.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *furai — the twin of English fore (before, forefather); governs dative and accusative. [wiktionary]

zug.etymology_derivation: Noun of ziehen (to pull — the tow/tug family): a train is 'the pull(er)', an elevator the Aufzug ('up-pull'). [wiktionary]

fahrt.etymology_derivation: Noun of fahren (fare): a 'faring' — a drive, ride, or voyage; the -t is the Germanic -þ nominal suffix. [wiktionary]

kaufen.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *kaupōną, borrowed from Latin caupō 'tradesman/innkeeper' — the same loan that gave English cheap; collateral cognates. [wiktionary]

gift.context_translation: The poison is in the glass!
gift.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *giftiz 'a giving/dose' — the true twin of gift; German kept the deadly-dose branch. Trap: das Gift = POISON. (Present: das Geschenk.) [wiktionary]

chef.context_translation: The boss is in the office.
chef.etymology_derivation: The true twin of chief (both from Latin caput via French) — but German kept the workplace sense. Trap: der Chef = BOSS. (Cook: der Koch.) [wiktionary]

handy.etymology_derivation: A German pseudo-Anglicism from 'hand(y)' coined in the 1990s. Trap: das Handy = MOBILE PHONE, not 'useful'. [wiktionary]

aktuell.etymology_derivation: Both from Latin actualis — true cognates, drifted senses. Trap: aktuell = CURRENT. (Actual: tatsächlich/wirklich.) [wiktionary]

rat.etymology_derivation: Ancient Germanic 'counsel' — the same root as 'read' (rædan, to advise!). Trap: der Rat = ADVICE. (Rodent: die Ratte.) [wiktionary]

brav.etymology_derivation: Both from Italian bravo — true cognates, drifted senses. Trap: brav = WELL-BEHAVED. (Brave: mutig.) [wiktionary]

fabrik.etymology_derivation: Both from Latin fabrica — true cognates, drifted senses. Trap: die Fabrik = FACTORY. (Fabric: der Stoff.) [wiktionary]

gymnasium.etymology_derivation: Both from the Greek wrestling-ground — true cognates, drifted senses. Trap: das Gymnasium = ACADEMIC HIGH SCHOOL. (Gym: die Turnhalle.) [wiktionary]

rente.etymology_derivation: Both from Latin rendere — true cognates, drifted senses. Trap: die Rente = PENSION. (Apartment rent: die Miete.) [wiktionary]

dom.etymology_derivation: Both from Latin domus (church-house) — true cognates, drifted senses. Trap: der Dom = CATHEDRAL. (Dome: die Kuppel.) [wiktionary]

art.context_phrase: Diese Art von Buch ist gut.
art.context_translation: This kind of book is good.
art.etymology_derivation: Both from Latin ars/artis — true cognates, drifted senses. Trap: die Art = KIND/TYPE. (Fine art: die Kunst.) [wiktionary]

fast.etymology_derivation: Ancient Germanic 'firmly, almost' — true cognate of fast in its 'firm' sense. Trap: fast = ALMOST. (Quick: schnell.) [wiktionary]

bald.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *balþaz — kin to English bold; the 'daring' became 'soon'. Trap: bald = SOON. (Hairless: kahl.) [wiktionary]

eventuell.etymology_derivation: Both from Latin eventus — true cognates, drifted senses. Trap: eventuell = POSSIBLY. (Eventually: schließlich/am Ende.) [wiktionary]

kaution.etymology_derivation: Both from Latin cautio — true cognates, drifted senses. Trap: die Kaution = SECURITY DEPOSIT. (Caution: die Vorsicht.) [wiktionary]

dein.etymology_derivation: The exact twin of thine (Proto-Germanic *þīnaz with th → d) — the KJV's 'thine' and 'mine eyes' are this word's living family. [wiktionary]

gabe.etymology_derivation: geben frozen into a noun — the true twin of English gift ('a giving'); verb and noun shared by both languages. [wiktionary]

in.etymology_derivation: The identical twin of in (Proto-Germanic *in); two-way preposition: motion → accusative, location → dative. [wiktionary]

auf.context_phrase: Das Buch ist auf dem Tisch.
auf.context_translation: The book is on the table.
auf.etymology_derivation: The twin of up/on (Proto-Germanic *ufa) — and the separable-prefix particle auf = up. [wiktionary]

hinter.context_phrase: Das Auto ist hinter dem Haus.
hinter.context_translation: The car is behind the house.
hinter.etymology_derivation: The twin of hind (as in hinder, behind) — *hinterą. Two-way preposition. [wiktionary]

neben.context_phrase: Die Katze schläft neben dem Sofa.
neben.context_translation: The cat sleeps beside the sofa.
neben.etymology_derivation: From the *nahuną 'near' family — kin to English nigh. Two-way preposition. [wiktionary]

zwischen.context_phrase: Der Ball ist zwischen den Büchern.
zwischen.context_translation: The ball is between the books.
zwischen.etymology_derivation: The twin of between (tw → zw + the same -en suffix): 'by-twain' ↔ 'two-ened'. Two-way preposition. [wiktionary]

stadt.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *stadiz — the twin of stead (homestead, instead); final d devoiced to [t]. [wiktionary]

schön.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *skauniz — the twin of archaic English sheen 'beautiful'. [wiktionary]

anrufen.etymology_derivation: Separable: an + rufen (to call/cry); rufen is kin to Old English hrōpan 'to shout'. [wiktionary]

verboten.etymology_derivation: ver- (for-) + bieten/bot — 'for-bidden' via the bid-root: bieten ↔ bid is the twin pair. [wiktionary]

auto.etymology_derivation: Short for Automobil — the same Greek autos ('self') loan as English auto, clipped German-style. [wiktionary]

klein.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *klainiz 'clean, fine' — the TRUE twin of English clean; the meaning drifted from 'clean' to 'small'. [wiktionary]

als.etymology_derivation: Kin to English else (both from the *alja- 'other' family) — the comparative particle. [wiktionary]

abend.context_phrase: Am Abend lese ich ein Buch.
abend.context_translation: In the evening I read a book.
abend.etymology_derivation: The twin of archaic English even/eve ('evening') — the same *ēbandaz root; Guten Abend keeps the wish-accusative. [wiktionary]

sehen.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *sehwaną — the identical twin of see (and gesehen ↔ seen); initial s voiced before vowels. [wiktionary]

vater.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *fadēr; English f ↔ German v=[f] reflects Verner's-law voicing, not the v→b shift family. [wiktionary]

mutter.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *mōdēr — English mother and German Mutter are essentially unchanged siblings. [wiktionary]

sohn.context_phrase: Mein Sohn ist sechs Jahre alt.
sohn.context_translation: My son is six years old.
sohn.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *sunuz — the direct twin of English son (the historical h was once pronounced). [wiktionary]

schwester.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *swestēr — sw- ↔ schw- beginning, otherwise essentially unchanged. [wiktionary]

eltern.etymology_derivation: Plural-only; a nominalized comparative of alt (old) — literally 'the elder ones', kin to English old. [wiktionary]

großvater.etymology_derivation: groß (big) + Vater; the Vater root is father via Verner's law, not V→B. [wiktionary]

großmutter.context_translation: My grandmother is baking a cake.
großmutter.etymology_derivation: groß (big) + Mutter; Mutter is the unchanged twin of English mother. [wiktionary]

oma.context_phrase: Meine Oma wohnt auf dem Land.
oma.context_translation: My grandma lives in the countryside.
oma.etymology_derivation: Nursery word, cognate only with Dutch oma; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

opa.etymology_derivation: Nursery word, cognate only with Dutch opa; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

onkel.context_phrase: Mein Onkel kommt morgen zu Besuch.
onkel.context_translation: My uncle is coming to visit tomorrow.
onkel.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from French oncle — the same French/Latin source as English uncle. [wiktionary]

tante.context_phrase: Meine Tante schenkt mir ein Buch.
tante.context_translation: My aunt is giving me a book.
tante.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from French tante; English aunt descends from the related Old French form. [wiktionary]

geschwister.etymology_derivation: ge- + Schwester — built on the same root as English sister (*swestēr). [wiktionary]

enkel.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *ankulaz 'ankle' — the same root as English ankle, meaning shifted to 'grandchild'. [wiktionary]

cousin.etymology_derivation: From Middle French cousin, Latin consobrinus — the shared Romance source of English cousin. [wiktionary]

cousine.etymology_derivation: From French cousine, Latin consobrina — shared Romance loan with English cousin. [wiktionary]

neffe.context_phrase: Mein Neffe ist zwei Jahre alt.
neffe.context_translation: My nephew is two years old.
neffe.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *nefô; English nephew is a Latin (nepos) loan — the same PIE kinship root. [wiktionary]

nichte.context_translation: My niece is playing in the garden.
nichte.etymology_derivation: This form replaced obsolete Niftel in the 17th century; English niece is a Latin loan of the same kinship root. [wiktionary]

schwager.context_phrase: Mein Schwager arbeitet bei einer Bank.
schwager.context_translation: My brother-in-law works at a bank.
schwager.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *swāgr 'husband's brother'; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

schwiegermutter.etymology_derivation: Schwieger (Old High German swigar; no English cognate) + Mutter, the twin of English mother. [wiktionary]

baby.context_translation: The baby is sleeping in the nursery.
baby.etymology_derivation: Mid-19th-century borrowing from English baby — a loan, not an inherited cognate. [wiktionary]

junge.etymology_derivation: Nominalized jung (young), Proto-Germanic *jungaz — the direct cognate of English young. [wiktionary]

mädchen.context_translation: The girl is reading a book.
mädchen.etymology_derivation: Magd (maid) + diminutive -chen; Magd and English maid share Proto-Germanic *magadiz. -chen is always neuter. [wiktionary]

familie.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from Latin familia — the same Latin source as English family. [wiktionary]

großeltern.etymology_derivation: groß (great) + Eltern (the elders); Eltern descends from alt, cognate with English old. [wiktionary]

rot.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *raudaz; English red is the same root — English d ↔ German t. [wiktionary]

blau.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *blēwaz; English blue (via French bleu) is the same Germanic word. [wiktionary]

grün.context_phrase: Im Sommer ist das Gras grün.
grün.context_translation: In summer the grass is green.
grün.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *grōniz, the root of grow; English green is the same Germanic word. [wiktionary]

schwarz.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *swartaz — the true English twin is swart/swarthy; English black is a different Germanic word. [wiktionary]

braun.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *brūn — English brown is the same Germanic word. [wiktionary]

grau.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *grāu — English gray is the same Germanic word. [wiktionary]

orange.etymology_derivation: French loan in both languages (ultimately Italian arancia) — a shared loan, no shift to fake. [wiktionary]

rosa.etymology_derivation: Latin rosa loaned by both languages — English pink via French rose, same Latin source. [wiktionary]

lila.etymology_derivation: From French lilas — a French loan in German; English lilac comes from the same French/Arabic source. [wiktionary]

bunt.etymology_derivation: Probably from Latin punctus, a relative of English point — no English color-word cognate; memorize this one. [wiktionary]

hell.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *halliz 'resounding'; English bright/light is not cognate — hell is akin to English hall. [wiktionary]

januar.etymology_derivation: Latin loan both English and German borrowed (via French): Latin Iānuārius. [wiktionary]

februar.etymology_derivation: Latin loan both English and German borrowed (via French): Latin Februārius. [wiktionary]

märz.etymology_derivation: Latin loan both languages share: Latin Martius via Middle High German merze. [wiktionary]

april.etymology_derivation: Latin loan both English and German borrowed (via French): Latin Aprīlis. [wiktionary]

mai.etymology_derivation: Latin loan both languages share: Latin (mensis) Maius via Middle High German meie. [wiktionary]

juni.etymology_derivation: Latin loan both English and German borrowed (via French): Latin Iūnius. [wiktionary]

juli.etymology_derivation: Latin loan both English and German borrowed (via French): Latin Iūlius. [wiktionary]

august.etymology_derivation: Latin loan both English and German borrowed (via French): Latin Augustus. [wiktionary]

september.etymology_derivation: Latin loan both languages share: Latin September, inherited via Middle High German. [wiktionary]

oktober.etymology_derivation: Latin loan both languages share: Latin Octōber, from octō 'eight' — the eighth month of the old Roman calendar. [wiktionary]

november.etymology_derivation: Latin loan both languages share: Latin November, inherited via Middle High German. [wiktionary]

dezember.etymology_derivation: Latin loan both languages share: Latin december, inherited via Middle High German. [wiktionary]

sommer.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *sumar — English summer is the same Germanic word. [wiktionary]

winter.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *wintruz — English winter is the same Germanic word. [wiktionary]

herbst.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *harbist — English harvest is the twin, with English v ↔ German b. [wiktionary]

frühling.etymology_derivation: A 15th-century formation from früh (early) + -ling; English spring is a different word — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

sonne.etymology_derivation: Old High German sunna — shares Proto-Germanic *sun(n)uz with English sun. [wiktionary]

mond.context_phrase: Der Mond ist heute Nacht hell.
mond.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *mānō — the same ancient moon-word as English moon. [wiktionary]

stern.context_phrase: Ich sehe einen Stern am Himmel.
stern.context_translation: I see a star in the sky.
stern.etymology_derivation: Old High German sterno — cognate with English star. [wiktionary]

himmel.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *himil — the same Germanic line as English heaven's root family. [wiktionary]

wolke.context_translation: A cloud is in the sky.
wolke.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *wolkn — the English cognate is archaic welkin 'sky'. [wiktionary]

regnen.context_translation: It is raining in Berlin today.
regnen.etymology_derivation: Denominal verb from Regen (rain, already known — the y→g twin of English rain). [wiktionary]

schneien.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *snīwaną — keeps the ancient sn- cluster shared with English snow. [wiktionary]

warm.etymology_derivation: Identical form and meaning as English warm since Old High German. [wiktionary]

kühl.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *kōluz — cognate with English cool (the umlaut is German's own). [wiktionary]

blitz.etymology_derivation: Old High German blëcchazzen — English bleak/bleach are the cognates; English blitz is a loan from German. [wiktionary]

trocken.etymology_derivation: Old High German truckan 'dry, parched' — related to English dry. [wiktionary]

nass.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *nat — cognate with Dutch nat; English wet is a translation match, not a cognate. [wiktionary]

frost.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *frost — the same word as English frost. [wiktionary]

nebel.context_phrase: Im Herbst gibt es oft Nebel.
nebel.context_translation: In autumn there is often fog.
nebel.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *nebulaz, from PIE *nébʰos — inherited Germanic, PIE-kin to English nebula. [wiktionary]

klima.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from Latin clima — a shared Latin loan both languages made separately. [wiktionary]

grad.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from French grade, Latin gradus 'a step' — the same Latin source as English grade/degree. [wiktionary]

scheinen.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *skīnan — class 1 strong verb (schien, geschienen), ablaut-matching shine/shone. [wiktionary]

deutschland.etymology_derivation: diutsch "of the people" + lant "land" — compound: land of the people. [wiktionary]

frankreich.etymology_derivation: Franke "Frank" + Reich "realm" — realm of the Franks. [wiktionary]

england.etymology_derivation: From Old English Engla land — land of the Angles. [wiktionary]

spanien.etymology_derivation: The same Latin name Hispania that English Spain descends from, via Old High German Spānia. [wiktionary]

italien.etymology_derivation: The same Latin name Italia as English Italy; shared proper name, no sound shift to fake. [wiktionary]

schweiz.etymology_derivation: die Schweiz is named after Schwyz, the canton the country takes its name from. [wiktionary]

österreich.etymology_derivation: Old element for "east" + rīhhi "realm" — the eastern realm (Reich ↔ rich). [wiktionary]

türkei.context_phrase: Der Urlaub war in der Türkei.
türkei.etymology_derivation: Land of the Turks: from Medieval Latin Turcia, influenced by Türke "Turk". [wiktionary]

polen.etymology_derivation: Middle High German Polen, plural of Pole — land of the Poles. [wiktionary]

amerika.etymology_derivation: The same name as English America; shared proper name. [wiktionary]

ukraine.etymology_derivation: The same name as English Ukraine; shared proper name. [wiktionary]

europa.etymology_derivation: Inherited from Middle High German Eurōpā — the same Greek name both languages share. [wiktionary]

japan.etymology_derivation: Via Dutch Japan from Malay Jepang, from Hokkien 日本 "sun origin" — the same route as English. [wiktionary]

irland.etymology_derivation: The same name as English Ireland — land of the Irish, shared proper name. [wiktionary]

land.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *landą — the identical twin of English land. [wiktionary]

lehrer.context_phrase: Der Lehrer kommt in die Klasse.
lehrer.context_translation: The teacher comes into the class.
lehrer.etymology_derivation: Agent noun of lehren (teach) + -er; lehren is cognate with English learn/lore. [wiktionary]

arzt.context_translation: The doctor helps me a lot.
arzt.etymology_derivation: From Middle High German arzet, from Latin archīāter (chief healer); no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

bäcker.etymology_derivation: Agent noun of backen (bake) + -er, Proto-Germanic *bakārijaz — the direct twin of English baker. [wiktionary]

koch.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *kok — a true k → ch shift word (cook ↔ Koch). [wiktionary]

verkäufer.context_phrase: Der Verkäufer zeigt mir die Schuhe.
verkäufer.context_translation: The salesman shows me the shoes.
verkäufer.etymology_derivation: Agent noun of verkaufen (sell, the kaufen/cheap family); English uses a different root for seller. [wiktionary]

polizist.context_phrase: Der Polizist fragt nach dem Weg.
polizist.context_translation: The policeman asks about the way.
polizist.etymology_derivation: Polizei + -ist, from Greek pólis via Latin polītīa — the same loan both languages share. [wiktionary]

schüler.etymology_derivation: From Medieval Latin scholaris — the same Latin loan that gave English scholar. [wiktionary]

student.etymology_derivation: From Medieval Latin studēns — a Latin loan both languages borrowed alike. [wiktionary]

fahrer.etymology_derivation: Agent noun of fahren (to fare/drive) + -er — the fare family again. [wiktionary]

sänger.etymology_derivation: Agent noun of singen (sing); initial s voices to [z] before vowels. [wiktionary]

bauer.context_phrase: Der Bauer wohnt auf dem Hof.
bauer.context_translation: The farmer lives on the farm.
bauer.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *būraz "dweller" — cognate with English boor, and with bower "dwelling". [wiktionary]

arbeiter.context_phrase: Der Arbeiter kommt um sieben Uhr.
arbeiter.context_translation: The worker comes at seven o'clock.
arbeiter.etymology_derivation: Agent noun of arbeiten (work) + -er; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

ingenieur.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from French ingénieur — the same French loan as English engineer. [wiktionary]

friseur.etymology_derivation: A French-style formation from frisieren; no standard English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

kopf.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *kuppaz 'round object'; originally a drinking vessel — cognate with archaic English cop. [wiktionary]

bein.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *bainą — the exact twin of English bone; German means leg. [wiktionary]

knie.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *knewą — the identical twin of English knee (silent k in both). [wiktionary]

hals.context_phrase: Sie trägt einen Schal um den Hals.
hals.context_translation: She wears a scarf around her neck.
hals.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *halsaz — Old English heals was the cognate; modern English neck is unrelated. [wiktionary]

rücken.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hrugjaz — the twin of English ridge; also the Rück- of zurückkommen. [wiktionary]

bauch.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *būkaz 'belly, body' — cognate with dialectal English bouk. [wiktionary]

magen.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *magō 'stomach' — related to English maw. [wiktionary]

blut.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *blōþą — the identical twin of English blood. [wiktionary]

haut.context_phrase: Die Haut brennt in der Sonne.
haut.context_translation: The skin burns in the sun.
haut.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hūdiz — the twin of English hide (and Dutch huid). [wiktionary]

haar.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *hār — the same word as English hair. [wiktionary]

knochen.context_phrase: Der Hund kaut an einem Knochen.
knochen.context_translation: The dog is chewing on a bone.
knochen.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *knokō 'bone, joint' — cognate with English knuckle; German k shifted to ch. [wiktionary]

ohr.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *ausô (Verner alternant) — the twin of English ear; Latin auris is PIE-kin. [wiktionary]

mund.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *munþaz — English kept the th, German hardened it to d. [wiktionary]

nase.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *nasō — English nose comes from an alternative Germanic form. [wiktionary]

schulter.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *skuldru — the twin of English shoulder. [wiktionary]

krank.context_phrase: Ich bin krank und bleibe zu Hause.
krank.context_translation: I am sick and staying home.
krank.etymology_derivation: Old sense 'crooked, weak' — Wiktionary: cognate with English crank. [wiktionary]

gesund.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *sundaz — the same root as English sound, as in safe and sound. [wiktionary]

schmerz.context_translation: I have pain in my back.
schmerz.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *smertan — cognate with English smart in its old 'sting' sense. [wiktionary]

fieber.context_translation: The child has a high fever.
fieber.etymology_derivation: Borrowed early from Latin febris — English fever shares the same Latin source via French. [wiktionary]

husten.context_phrase: Ich trinke Tee gegen den Husten.
husten.context_translation: I am drinking tea for the cough.
husten.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *hwōstō; no English cognate listed — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

schuh.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *skōh — the true twin of English shoe (see Handschuh, hand-shoe). [wiktionary]

hut.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hōdaz — Wiktionary's English cognate is hood, not hat. See Fingerhut. [wiktionary]

hemd.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *hamiþi; English shirt is from a different root — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

rock.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hrukkaz; English skirt is from a different root — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

mantel.etymology_derivation: From Late Latin mantellum, ultimately Gaulish — a Romance loan; no English cognate. [wiktionary]

stiefel.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from Old French estivel; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

kleid.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *klaiþą — English cloth is the cognate: English th ↔ German d. [wiktionary]

hose.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *hosā — the same Germanic source as English hose (hosiery). [wiktionary]

socke.etymology_derivation: West Germanic borrowing from Latin soccus 'slipper' — a parallel borrowing with English sock. [wiktionary]

tasche.etymology_derivation: Perhaps Proto-Germanic *taskǭ; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

t-shirt.etymology_derivation: Borrowed directly from English t-shirt — an English loan in German. [wiktionary]

jacke.etymology_derivation: From Middle French jaque (from the name Jacques) — the same French source as English jacket. [wiktionary]

mütze.etymology_derivation: From Medieval Latin almutia 'hood, cowl' — a Romance loan; no English cognate. [wiktionary]

brille.etymology_derivation: From Latin beryllus 'beryl' — the gemstone lenses were first made of; no standard English cognate. [wiktionary]

gürtel.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *gurdilaz — English girdle is the true cognate. [wiktionary]

schal.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from English shawl, from Persian šâl — a loan, not an inherited cognate. [wiktionary]

knopf.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *knuppaz 'lump'; English button is unrelated — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

links.context_translation: The bank is on the left.
links.etymology_derivation: Middle High German linkes; only Dutch links is a cognate — no English cognate, memorize this one. [wiktionary]

rechts.context_translation: The car is on the right.
rechts.etymology_derivation: recht + adverbial -s; recht is the direct cognate of English right (Recht, already known). [wiktionary]

geradeaus.context_phrase: Gehen Sie geradeaus bis zur Ecke.
geradeaus.context_translation: Go straight ahead to the corner.
geradeaus.etymology_derivation: gerade + aus fused into one adverb; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

oben.context_phrase: Das Buch ist oben auf dem Tisch.
oben.context_translation: The book is up on the table.
oben.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *ubanē, kin to über (over); no direct English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

unten.etymology_derivation: Old High German undenân, kin to unter (under); no direct English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

ecke.context_translation: I am waiting at the corner.
ecke.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *agjō — the same word as English edge. [wiktionary]

hier.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *hēr — the explicit cognate of English here. [wiktionary]

nähe.context_phrase: In der Nähe gibt es einen Markt.
nähe.etymology_derivation: nah + -e; nah is the twin of archaic English nigh. [wiktionary]

weit.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *wīdaz — the direct cognate of English wide. [wiktionary]

fern.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *ferrai — the same word as English far (see der Fernseher, far-seer). [wiktionary]

mitte.context_phrase: Ich wohne in der Mitte der Stadt.
mitte.context_translation: I live in the middle of the city.
mitte.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *midjǭ — cognate with English mid (see Mittwoch, mid-week). [wiktionary]

geld.context_translation: I have no money with me.
geld.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *geldą 'reward, payment' — kin to English geld and yield, NOT to gold. [wiktionary]

kosten.context_translation: How much does the bread cost?
kosten.etymology_derivation: Latin loan via Old French coster, from Latin cōnstō — the same Romance source as English cost. [wiktionary]

zahlen.context_translation: I would like to pay, please.
zahlen.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *talōną 'to count' — cognate with English tale; German z is the shifted t. [wiktionary]

bezahlen.etymology_derivation: be- + zahlen — the inseparable prefix at work on the tale-family verb. [wiktionary]

billig.etymology_derivation: Old High German billīh 'appropriate', kin to Bild/bilden; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

teuer.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *diurijaz — the true twin of English dear (d → t). [wiktionary]

euro.etymology_derivation: Clipping of Europa — the same root as English Europe. [wiktionary]

cent.context_phrase: Das gibt es für fünfzig Cent.
cent.context_translation: You can get that for fifty cents.
cent.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from English cent — a shared modern coinage. [wiktionary]

kasse.context_phrase: Bitte zahlen Sie an der Kasse.
kasse.etymology_derivation: From Italian cassa, Latin capsa — the same Latin root behind English case and cash. [wiktionary]

preis.etymology_derivation: Ultimately from Latin pretium — the same source as English price (and prize). [wiktionary]

markt.context_phrase: Auf dem Markt kaufe ich Obst.
markt.context_translation: At the market I buy fruit.
markt.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *markat, an early Latin borrowing shared with English market. [wiktionary]

geschenk.etymology_derivation: ge- + schenken (pour, serve); no English cognate — memorize this one (das Gift is the trap word). [wiktionary]

günstig.context_translation: This hotel is very good value.
günstig.etymology_derivation: Gunst (favor) + -ig; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

fleisch.context_phrase: Ich esse gern Fleisch mit Kartoffeln.
fleisch.context_translation: I like eating meat with potatoes.
fleisch.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *flaiski — the exact counterpart of English flesh. [wiktionary]

ei.context_phrase: Ich esse ein Ei zum Frühstück.
ei.context_translation: I eat an egg for breakfast.
ei.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *aij — Wiktionary lists English ey and egg as cognates. [wiktionary]

käse.context_phrase: Der Käse auf dem Brot ist lecker.
käse.context_translation: The cheese on the bread is tasty.
käse.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *kāsī, borrowed early from Latin cāseus — shared with English cheese. [wiktionary]

wurst.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *wursti; English wurst is only a later borrowing from German — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

suppe.etymology_derivation: Borrowed via Middle Low German suppe under French influence — both trace to Proto-Germanic *supô 'broth'. [wiktionary]

salat.etymology_derivation: 15th-century borrowing from Italian salata — the same Romance source as English salad. [wiktionary]

gemüse.etymology_derivation: From Old High German muos 'food, porridge'; English mush is only a possible cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

obst.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *obaet; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

kartoffel.etymology_derivation: From Tartuffel, from Italian tartufolo 'truffle', Latin terrae tūber 'earth tuber'; no English cognate. [wiktionary]

reis.etymology_derivation: Borrowed via Late Latin rīsum, Greek órūza — the same trade-route loan as English rice. [wiktionary]

kuchen.context_translation: Would you like a piece of cake?
kuchen.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *kōkô; Wiktionary names only Dutch koek — see Apfelkuchen. [wiktionary]

zucker.context_phrase: Ich nehme Zucker in den Kaffee.
zucker.context_translation: I take sugar in my coffee.
zucker.etymology_derivation: Via Italian zucchero from Arabic sukkar, Sanskrit śárkarā — the same trade-route loan as English sugar. [wiktionary]

honig.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *hunag — Wiktionary: 'Cognate with English honey'. [wiktionary]

zwiebel.etymology_derivation: Borrowed early from Late Latin cēpulla; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

tomate.context_phrase: Die Tomate ist rot und reif.
tomate.context_translation: The tomato is red and ripe.
tomate.etymology_derivation: From Spanish/French tomate, Classical Nahuatl tomatl — the same New World loan as English tomato. [wiktionary]

gurke.context_phrase: Die Gurke ist frisch und grün.
gurke.context_translation: The cucumber is fresh and green.
gurke.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from Old Polish ogórek, Greek angoúrion — cognate with English gherkin. [wiktionary]

karotte.context_phrase: Die Karotte ist orange und gesund.
karotte.context_translation: The carrot is orange and healthy.
karotte.etymology_derivation: From French carotte, Latin carōta, Greek kărōtón — the same Greco-Latin source as English carrot. [wiktionary]

birne.context_phrase: Ich esse eine Birne zum Nachtisch.
birne.context_translation: I eat a pear for dessert.
birne.etymology_derivation: From Vulgar Latin pira, plural of Latin pirum; also the 'bulb' of die Glühbirne. [wiktionary]

erdbeere.context_phrase: Die Erdbeere schmeckt im Sommer süß.
erdbeere.context_translation: The strawberry tastes sweet in summer.
erdbeere.etymology_derivation: Erde (earth) + Beere (berry) — 'earth berry'; the Beere element parallels English berry. [wiktionary]

saft.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *sap 'juice, sap' — matching English sap. [wiktionary]

frühstück.context_phrase: Das Frühstück ist um sieben Uhr.
frühstück.etymology_derivation: Literally 'early piece (bite)': früh + Stück; NOT the break-fast calque English uses. [wiktionary]

abendessen.context_phrase: Das Abendessen ist um acht Uhr.
abendessen.etymology_derivation: Abend (evening) + Essen (meal) — a transparent compound of known parts. [wiktionary]

backen.context_phrase: Ich backe einen Kuchen für dich.
backen.context_translation: I'm baking a cake for you.
backen.etymology_derivation: Old High German backan — explicit cognate of English bake (see der Bäcker). [wiktionary]

schmecken.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *smakkijan — Wiktionary: 'Compare English smack and smatch'. [wiktionary]

immer.context_phrase: Ich trinke immer Kaffee am Morgen.
immer.context_translation: I always drink coffee in the morning.
immer.etymology_derivation: OHG iomēr 'ever + more' — cognate with Middle English 'a mare' (evermore). [wiktionary]

nie.context_phrase: Ich habe nie Zeit am Montag.
nie.context_translation: I never have time on Monday.
nie.etymology_derivation: MHG nie, OHG nio; thin etymology on Wiktionary. [UNVERIFIED — check] [wiktionary]

manchmal.context_translation: Sometimes I go to the cinema.
manchmal.etymology_derivation: manch (many a) + Mal (time, the meal-word cousin) — 'many a time'. [wiktionary]

oft.context_translation: We often play in the park.
oft.etymology_derivation: Old High German ofta — the true twin of English oft/often. [wiktionary]

später.etymology_derivation: Comparative of spät (late); no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

sofort.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from Middle Low German so vōrt — literally 'so forth', mirroring the English phrase. [wiktionary]

früh.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *frō(ī); only Dutch/Low German cognates listed. [UNVERIFIED — check] [wiktionary]

spät.context_phrase: Es ist schon spät in der Nacht.
spät.context_translation: It is already late at night.
spät.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *spādī; only Dutch/Low German cognates — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

jetzt.etymology_derivation: Old High German iozuo, je (ever) + zu (to); no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

minute.etymology_derivation: Medieval Latin minūta — the same Latin loan as English minute. [wiktionary]

stunde.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *stundu — cognate with archaic English stound 'hour'. [wiktionary]

monat.etymology_derivation: The twin of English month, from *mānōþ 'moon' (see der Mond) — th→d included. [wiktionary]

jahr.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *jār — the twin of English year. [wiktionary]

moment.etymology_derivation: From Latin momentum — the same Latin loan as English moment. [wiktionary]

dauern.etymology_derivation: From Latin dūrō via Middle Low German — kin to archaic English dure, as in endure. [wiktionary]

null.etymology_derivation: From Italian nulla, Latin nullus 'none' — the same Latin loan as English null. [wiktionary]

eins.context_translation: I have only one of those.
eins.etymology_derivation: Contraction of eines, Proto-Germanic *ainaz — the twin of English one (see ein). [wiktionary]

vier.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *feuwar — the direct twin of English four. [wiktionary]

fünf.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *fimf, PIE *pénkʷe — the twin of English five. [wiktionary]

sechs.context_translation: It is six o'clock in the morning.
sechs.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *sehs, PIE *swéḱs — the same root as English six. [wiktionary]

neun.context_phrase: Das Kind ist neun Jahre alt.
neun.context_translation: The child is nine years old.
neun.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *newun — the direct twin of English nine. [wiktionary]

zehn.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *tehun — the twin of English ten with the classic t → z shift. [wiktionary]

dreizehn.shift_rule: TH → D + T → S / SS / Z
dreizehn.context_phrase: Mein Sohn ist dreizehn Jahre alt.
dreizehn.context_translation: My son is thirteen years old.
dreizehn.etymology_derivation: drei + zehn — thirteen with a double shift: th → d and t → z. [wiktionary]

hundert.context_phrase: Ein Jahr hat nicht hundert Tage.
hundert.context_translation: A year does not have a hundred days.
hundert.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hundaradą 'hundred-count' — the twin of English hundred. [wiktionary]

million.context_phrase: Die Stadt hat eine Million Menschen.
million.context_translation: The city has one million people.
million.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from Italian millione — the same Italian loan as English million. [wiktionary]

vierzig.context_phrase: Mein Vater ist vierzig Jahre alt.
vierzig.context_translation: My father is forty years old.
vierzig.etymology_derivation: vier + -zig; -zig is German's ancient -ty (Proto-Germanic *tigiwiz) — forty with t → z. [wiktionary]

fünfzig.context_phrase: Die Frau ist fünfzig Jahre alt.
fünfzig.context_translation: The woman is fifty years old.
fünfzig.etymology_derivation: fünf + -zig — fifty with the same -ty twin suffix and the t → z shift. [wiktionary]

zimmer.context_phrase: Mein Zimmer ist groß und hell.
zimmer.context_translation: My room is big and bright.
zimmer.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *timrą — cognate with English timber: English keeps t, German shifted it to z. [wiktionary]

fenster.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *fenestr, an early borrowing of Latin fenestra — a Latin loan both languages share. [wiktionary]

bett.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *badją — explicitly cognate with English bed; the High German d→t gives the final -tt. [wiktionary]

stuhl.context_translation: The chair stands at the table.
stuhl.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *stōl — cognate with English stool; the meaning narrowed from stool to chair. [wiktionary]

wand.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *wanduz 'fence' — Wiktionary: cognate with English wand, not wall. [wiktionary]

boden.context_translation: The floor is made of wood.
boden.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *budm-, variant of *butmaz — explicitly cognate with English bottom. [wiktionary]

lampe.context_phrase: Die Lampe steht auf dem Tisch.
lampe.context_translation: The lamp is on the table.
lampe.etymology_derivation: From Latin lampada — the same Latin loan as English lamp. [wiktionary]

decke.etymology_derivation: Via decken 'to cover', Proto-Germanic *þakjaną — cognate with English deck, related to thatch. [wiktionary]

sofa.context_translation: The sofa is in the living room.
sofa.etymology_derivation: From French sofa, ultimately Arabic ṣuffa — the same loan route as English sofa. [wiktionary]

schlüssel.context_phrase: Der Schlüssel ist auf dem Tisch.
schlüssel.context_translation: The key is on the table.
schlüssel.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *slutil, kin to schließen (close) — cognate with English slot. [wiktionary]

spiegel.context_phrase: Der Spiegel hängt an der Wand.
spiegel.context_translation: The mirror hangs on the wall.
spiegel.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *spēgl, an early adoption of Latin speculum; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

balkon.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from French balcon, Italian balcone — a Romance loan; no Germanic root. [wiktionary]

vorhang.etymology_derivation: vor (in front) + hängen (hang) — 'the front-hang'; no English cognate. [wiktionary]

teppich.context_phrase: Der Teppich liegt unter dem Tisch.
teppich.context_translation: The rug is under the table.
teppich.etymology_derivation: Via Medieval Latin tapicus, from Latin tapes; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

schrank.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *skrankaz 'grid, barrier'; no English cognate — memorize this one (see der Kühlschrank). [wiktionary]

wohnen.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *wunāną, from the 'wish, love' root; no English cognate named on Wiktionary. [wiktionary]

lesen.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *lesaną 'to gather' — cognate with archaic English lease 'to glean'; reading is gathering words. [wiktionary]

tanzen.etymology_derivation: From Old French dancer via Low German — the same French loan as English dance. [wiktionary]

musik.etymology_derivation: From Latin mūsica — the same Latin loan as English music. [wiktionary]

kino.context_translation: We are going to the cinema.
kino.etymology_derivation: Clipping of Kinematograph, the Greek-rooted invention name — a shared international loan. [wiktionary]

film.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from English film — a direct English loan into German. [wiktionary]

sport.etymology_derivation: 19th-century borrowing from English sport — see treiben (to drive) in Ich treibe Sport. [wiktionary]

spiel.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *spil 'dance'; no English cognate — English spiel is borrowed FROM German. [wiktionary]

lied.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *leuþ 'song'; no modern English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

fußball.etymology_derivation: Fuß + Ball — a calque of English football; Fuß is foot with the t→s shift. [wiktionary]

malen.etymology_derivation: From Mal 'spot, mark'; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

klavier.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from French clavier, from Latin clavis 'key' — a Romance loan. [wiktionary]

party.etymology_derivation: Unadapted borrowing from English party — a doublet of older loans Partei/Partie. [wiktionary]

hund.context_phrase: Der Hund schläft auf dem Sofa.
hund.context_translation: The dog sleeps on the sofa.
hund.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hundaz — cognate with English hound, the same ancient dog-word. [wiktionary]

vogel.context_translation: The bird sings in the garden.
vogel.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *fuglaz, likely from 'to fly' — cognate with English fowl. [wiktionary]

kuh.context_phrase: Die Kuh steht auf der Weide.
kuh.context_translation: The cow stands in the meadow.
kuh.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *kōz, PIE *gʷṓws — the twin of English cow. [wiktionary]

schwein.context_phrase: Das Schwein lebt auf dem Bauernhof.
schwein.context_translation: The pig lives on the farm.
schwein.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *swīn — the twin of English swine. [wiktionary]

bär.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *berô — literally 'the brown one', a taboo-avoidance word; twin of English bear. [wiktionary]

ente.context_phrase: Die Ente schwimmt auf dem See.
ente.context_translation: The duck swims on the lake.
ente.etymology_derivation: Middle High German ente; only Dutch eend is a cognate — no English cognate. [wiktionary]

löwe.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *lewo; only Dutch leeuw named — no English cognate, memorize this one. [wiktionary]

baum.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *baumaz — English beam is the cognate; a beam was originally a tree. [wiktionary]

blume.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *blōmō 'blossom'; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

wald.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *walþu — cognate with Old English weald, surviving in weald/wold. [wiktionary]

blatt.context_translation: The leaf falls from the tree.
blatt.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *bladą 'leaf' — English blade is the same word, meanings split. [wiktionary]

feuer.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *fuir, PIE *péh₂wr̥ — English fire is the explicit cognate (see Feuerzeug). [wiktionary]

luft.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *luftuz; Old English lyft and Icelandic loft compared, modern twin unconfirmed. [UNVERIFIED — check] [wiktionary]

freund.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *frijōndz, 'the loving one' — the exact twin of English friend. [wiktionary]

herr.context_translation: The gentleman is called Mr. Müller.
herr.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hairaz 'grey' — the grey-haired one, cognate with English hoar. [wiktionary]

dame.etymology_derivation: From French dame, Latin domina — Wiktionary: 'Cognate with English dame'. [wiktionary]

mensch.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *manniskaz 'human', built on Mann — English mannish is the cognate form. [wiktionary]

schule.context_phrase: Die Schule beginnt um acht Uhr.
schule.etymology_derivation: From Latin (ultimately Greek scholē) — the same classical loan as English school; see Schüler. [wiktionary]

bahnhof.etymology_derivation: Bahn (track) + Hof (yard) — the track-yard; a transparent compound of German parts. [wiktionary]

flughafen.etymology_derivation: Flug (flight) + Hafen (port) — the flight-port; see der Fernseher-style calques. [wiktionary]

hotel.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from French hôtel — the same French loan as English hotel. [wiktionary]

urlaub.context_phrase: Ich fahre im Urlaub nach Italien.
urlaub.context_translation: I go to Italy on vacation.
urlaub.etymology_derivation: Middle High German urloup 'permission to be away', kin to erlauben — cognate with English leave. [wiktionary]

wir.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *wīz — the very same pronoun as English we. [wiktionary]

uns.etymology_derivation: The accusative/dative of wir — the same West Germanic pronoun as English us. [wiktionary]

jung.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *jungaz — the twin of English young (see der Junge). [wiktionary]

schlecht.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *slihtaz 'smooth, level' — Wiktionary: cognate with English slight. [wiktionary]

lang.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *langaz — the identical twin of English long. [wiktionary]

kurz.etymology_derivation: From Latin curtus — the same Latin word as English curt; NOT related to short. [wiktionary]

leicht.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *linhtaz — English light is the explicit cognate: gh ↔ ch. [wiktionary]

schwer.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *swēraz 'heavy, grave'; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

richtig.etymology_derivation: recht (right, the gh→ch twin) + -ig — 'right-y', the same root as English right. [wiktionary]

falsch.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *falskī, from Latin falsus — the same Latin line as English false. [wiktionary]

sauber.etymology_derivation: Ultimately from Latin sobrius — the same Latin word behind English sober. [wiktionary]

laut.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *hlūd; only Old Saxon hlūd compared — the loud link is not on the page. [wiktionary]

leise.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *līs(ī) 'low, soft'; no cognates named — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

voll.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *fullaz — English full is the explicit cognate. [wiktionary]

leer.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *lēziz — English leer is the listed cognate, both originally 'empty'. [wiktionary]

offen.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *opan — English open is listed among cognates, kin to auf. [wiktionary]

glücklich.etymology_derivation: Glück (luck) + -lich; Wiktionary: 'Compare English luck' — a relative via Dutch. [wiktionary]

müde.context_phrase: Ich bin müde und gehe ins Bett.
müde.context_translation: I am tired and go to bed.
müde.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *mōþī; only Dutch moe named — no English cognate, memorize this one. [wiktionary]

traurig.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *dreuzagaz — English dreary is the cognate, with English d ↔ German t. [wiktionary]

wütend.context_phrase: Er ist wütend auf seinen Bruder.
wütend.context_translation: He is angry at his brother.
wütend.etymology_derivation: wüten (to rage, the Wut family) + -end; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

angst.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *angustiz; the page names no English cognate (anguish/angry not cited) — treat as memorize. [wiktionary]

lust.context_translation: I feel like having ice cream.
lust.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *lustuz — the explicit twin of English lust; in German it just means desire (Lust haben). [wiktionary]

froh.context_phrase: Ich bin froh, dass du kommst.
froh.context_translation: I am glad that you are coming.
froh.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *frawaz 'quick, glad' — English frolic (via Dutch) is the named cognate. [wiktionary]

liebe.context_phrase: Die Liebe ist wichtig im Leben.
liebe.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *lubō — the explicit twin of English love; the noun of lieben. [wiktionary]

nett.etymology_derivation: From Old French net, Latin nitidus — Wiktionary: 'Compare English neat', a shared Romance loan. [wiktionary]

langweilig.etymology_derivation: Langeweile (long while) + -ig — literally 'long-while-ish'; no English cognate. [wiktionary]

nervös.context_phrase: Ich bin nervös vor der Prüfung.
nervös.context_translation: I am nervous before the exam.
nervös.etymology_derivation: From Latin nervōsus — the same Latin loan as English nervous. [wiktionary]

stolz.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *stultaz 'proud, stiff' — English stout is the named cognate. [wiktionary]

freude.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *frawiþō, from the 'jump for joy' root; only Dutch cognates named — see Schadenfreude. [wiktionary]

glück.etymology_derivation: Probably borrowed from Old Dutch *gilukki — Wiktionary: 'Compare English luck' (a relative via Dutch). [wiktionary]

ja.context_translation: Yes, I am happy to come along.
ja.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *ja; the German section names only Yiddish — the yea link is not on the page. [UNVERIFIED — check] [wiktionary]

nein.context_translation: No, I do not have time.
nein.etymology_derivation: ni + ein, 'not one' — the same contraction story as English none/no from Old English nān. [wiktionary]

danke.etymology_derivation: Ellipsis of ich danke dir — the same danken already known (the think/thank family, th→d). [wiktionary]

bitte.etymology_derivation: Ellipsis of ich bitte (I beg you), from bitten 'to ask'; no cognate supported on the page. [wiktionary]

entschuldigung.context_translation: Excuse me, where is the station?
entschuldigung.etymology_derivation: entschuldigen + -ung — the 'un-guilting' noun; the page names no English cognates. [wiktionary]

vielleicht.etymology_derivation: Middle High German vil līchte 'very easily' — its second element is the ancestor of leicht. [wiktionary]

genau.context_phrase: Die Uhr zeigt genau drei Uhr.
genau.context_translation: The clock shows exactly three o'clock.
genau.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hnawwaz 'close, niggardly' — archaic Old English hnēaw is the named cognate. [wiktionary]

natürlich.context_translation: Of course I will gladly help you.
natürlich.etymology_derivation: Natur + -lich — Wiktionary cross-references English naturally; the same classical loan line. [wiktionary]

tschüss.etymology_derivation: CONFIRMED: Low German adjüs, from Dutch adjuus, from French adieu / Spanish adiós — 'to God' worn down to bye. [wiktionary]

hilfe.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *helpō, from helpaną (to help, already known) — the ancestor of English help. [wiktionary]

willkommen.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *wiljakumô, 'the wished come' — the explicit cognate of English welcome. [wiktionary]

heißen.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *haitaną — archaic English hight 'was named' is the verified cognate (also behest). [wiktionary]

buchstabieren.etymology_derivation: Buchstabe (letter, 'book-staff') + -ieren — a native root with the Latin-style -ieren verb suffix. [wiktionary]

freuen.etymology_derivation: froh (glad) + -en — froh from Old High German frō, Proto-Germanic *frawaz 'quick, glad'; the English relative is frolic, borrowed from Dutch vrolijk 'joy-ly'. Reflexive: sich freuen. [wiktionary]

fühlen.etymology_derivation: Old High German fuolen, from Proto-West Germanic *fōlijan 'to feel' — the exact twin of English feel (Old English fēlan). Reflexive: sich fühlen. [wiktionary]

anziehen.english_cognate: to put on / get dressed (an + ziehen)
anziehen.english_meaning: to put on / get dressed (an + ziehen)
anziehen.etymology_derivation: Separable: an ('on') + ziehen ('pull' — the tow/tug family, already known): to pull on. Reflexive sich anziehen = get dressed. [wiktionary]

wenn.context_phrase: Wenn ich Zeit habe, lese ich.
wenn.context_translation: When(ever) I have time, I read.
wenn.etymology_derivation: Old High German hwanne, from Proto-West Germanic *hwan — the exact twin of English when and the etymological doublet of German wann: wann asks the question, wenn builds the clause. [wiktionary]

ob.context_phrase: Ich weiß nicht, ob er kommt.
ob.context_translation: I do not know whether he is coming.
ob.etymology_derivation: From Old High German oba, from Proto-Germanic *jabai 'when, if' — the true cognate of English if (both carry the same ancient labial). [wiktionary]

banane.context_phrase: Ich esse eine Banane zum Frühstück.
banane.context_translation: I eat a banana for breakfast.
banane.etymology_derivation: Borrowed in the 16th century from Portuguese banana, from a West African language; English banana is the same borrowing. [wiktionary]

zitrone.context_phrase: Der Tee mit Zitrone schmeckt gut.
zitrone.context_translation: The tea with lemon tastes good.
zitrone.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from Italian citrone and Middle French citron, from Latin citrus; English citron and citrus come from the same Latin word. [wiktionary]

kirsche.etymology_derivation: From West Germanic kirsija, an early borrowing of Late Latin ceresia; English cherry comes from the same Latin word, its ch being a later English palatalization. [wiktionary]

pfirsich.etymology_derivation: From West Germanic persik, from Late Latin persicum, meaning Persian apple; English peach descends from the same Latin word, with p corresponding to German pf. [wiktionary]

wassermelone.context_translation: The watermelon is in the fridge.
wassermelone.etymology_derivation: Compound of Wasser and Melone; Wasser corresponds to English water via the t to ss shift, and Melone matches English melon, both from Late Latin melo. [wiktionary]

melone.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from Italian melone and Middle French melon, from Late Latin melo, short for Latin melopepo, from Greek; English melon is the same loan. [wiktionary]

nuss.context_phrase: Der Kuchen hat Nüsse und Schokolade.
nuss.context_translation: The cake has nuts and chocolate.
nuss.etymology_derivation: From Proto-Germanic hnuts; English nut is a direct cognate, with the Germanic t appearing as ss in German and the old initial h dropped. [wiktionary]

paprika.context_phrase: Ich nehme Paprika für den Salat.
paprika.context_translation: I am taking paprika for the salad.
paprika.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from Hungarian paprika, from Serbo-Croatian, ultimately from Latin piper, meaning pepper; English paprika is a parallel borrowing. [wiktionary]

bohne.etymology_derivation: From Proto-Germanic bauno; English bean is a direct cognate with the same meaning. [wiktionary]

mais.context_translation: The corn grows in the garden.
mais.etymology_derivation: From Spanish maíz, from Taíno mahis; English maize is the same borrowing, while corn is the everyday English name. [wiktionary]

kohl.etymology_derivation: From Old High German kol, an early borrowing of Latin caulis, meaning stalk or cabbage stem; English kale and cole descend from the same Latin word. [wiktionary]

pilz.context_translation: The mushroom grows in the forest.
pilz.etymology_derivation: From West Germanic bulit, an early borrowing of Latin boletus, the porcini mushroom; English bolete is a direct loan of the same Latin word. [wiktionary]

knoblauch.context_phrase: Ich gebe Knoblauch in die Soße.
knoblauch.context_translation: I add garlic to the sauce.
